name: Sun Deck
blocked: Restaurant's own listing (SinglePlatform widget embedded on hoteldel.com/dine/sun-deck/, data-location="sundeck") renders the full item list (Main Menu, Cocktails/Wine/Beer, Kids Menu, ~50+ items) but with prices stripped server-side -- only one item (a Summer Special, Birria Nachos GF and Draft Beer, $34) carries a price in the HTML; grepping the whole widget response for "price" finds nothing else. The Hilton mirror (hilton.com/en/hotels/sanqqqq-hotel-del-coronado/dining/sun-deck/) 403s a browser-UA curl. The only other source found, a menuweb.menu-hosted PDF, is a directory-farm aggregation with garbled section names ("Indian", "Mexican Dishes", "Ingredients Used", "Restaurant Category: BAR") and prices visibly misaligned to the wrong dish names -- fails the pairing-confidence bar, not used. Needs a Chrome-equipped agent to check whether hoteldel.com renders per-item prices through interaction/JS the static SinglePlatform payload omits, or to load hilton.com past its bot gate.
notes: Categories reached: Main Menu (For The Table, Salads & Bowls, Handhelds, Sides, Kids Bites, Seaside Sweets), Cocktails/Wine/Beer (Signature Cocktails, Wine, On Tap, Cans, Signature Mocktails). All read but unpriced except the one special noted above.

name: Petes Place
blocked: The listed domain petesplacelamesa.com is dead: the root redirects (via 302) to a Network Solutions parked-domain page (networksolutions.com/typepad?siteID=100...), and the /petes_place/ path redirects to /lander (a domain-parking landing page) over plain HTTP while HTTPS 403s behind Cloudflare. Directory alternatives found by search (zmenu.com, menupix.com) both 403 a curl request; restaurantji.com loads but contains no prices, only reviews; restaurantguru.com's only dollar figure is a $20-$30 per-person price-range badge, not per-item prices. Yelp (m.yelp.com/biz/petes-place-la-mesa) 403s -- its dated photos of the physical menu would be an allowed source per the playbook but require a browser to view. Needs a Chrome-equipped agent to check Yelp/Google Maps photos for a dated shot of the actual posted menu, and to verify via search whether the business has moved to a different live domain or Facebook page.
notes: No section list established -- could not reach any source with the restaurant's real menu structure. WebSearch summary described a bar-food/breakfast menu (burgers, wings, nachos, Country Benedict, Sausage Gravy & Biscuits, tacos, 20 beers on tap) but this is unverified against raw bytes and not used for dishes per playbook rule 4.

name: La Bella Cafe & Games
notes: Site branding calls this location "La Bella Pizza" (the restaurant group's shared name across its two Chula Vista locations), but the address 289 G Street, Chula Vista, CA 91910 matches the work list exactly, and the Popmenu location record's own name field is literally "La Bella Cafe & Games" (location id 5565, phone (619) 426-8830) -- distinct from the other location "La Bella Pizza Garden" at 373 Third Avenue (id 5560). Used the EXACT work-list name per house rules despite the page chrome saying "La Bella Pizza". Categories reached: Appetizers, Soups & Salads, Our Famous Pizza, Dinners, Pasta Dishes, Sandwiches, Family Meals & Pizza Party Combo, Dishes Served Family/Half Catering Trays, Desserts -- all 9 sections of the "Dine In Take-Out Delivery" menu (the complete core food menu). A separate "Craft Brew & Fine Wines" menu (beer taps + wine list, adjunct) rendered 0 items server-side for this location -- checked, not core, excluded. A "Catering" menu tab also exists and was not opened (adjunct to the dine-in menu, which already includes a family/catering-tray section). Prices for items with a single size came straight from the page's JSON-LD (schema.org Menu, 48 items). The other 34 items use Popmenu's per-size pricing (wings, pizzas by size, pasta plate/platter, catering trays) which is absent from the section JSON-LD (offers: null) and only appears in each item's own page under window.POPMENU_APOLLO_STATE (MenuItem.sizes -> MenuItemSize.price) -- fetched all 34 item pages individually and expanded each size into its own dish row, e.g. "Original Buffalo Wings (Small)" / "(Large)".
